chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Stepfather as master baker, hunter and fisherman
summary: His stepfather was an oven man and expert on the lake and weather; Danny had Creole food with one side and country food with the other.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So he and I, we took up right away. He was a master baker, which is called... He was an oven man, which is the baker that goes to the oven, raises up the hood and puts the bread in and takes the bread out. Time. It's got to be timed perfectly, or you lose a batch. I should have been a baker. But I wrapped bread for a while. You'd wrap the bread... They'd bring it out, you'd let it cool, then you'd wrap it.

He was a master baker. He was a master hunter. He was a master fisherman. He knew all about the water. If we were going fishing, we'd go out on a lake, if you heard a skip(?), he'd say, "Come on, let's go. There's a Northeastern coming in, or a Northwestern." And sure enough, off on the horizon he would see the darkness, and next thing you know, you'd see that water doing the chopping." Then we'd get to land, where we may have been a block out in the water, and get to the land just in time, or that water start choppin' and turn that boat over. He was great.

Yeah. His brother was... There was brother who had a camp on the lake, dealt from it all his life. Dealt in fish and crabs for the restaurants in town. So while I had Creole food with my French people, my mother's people, and I had Country food with my grandmother and my father's people. They came out of New Iberia. I'll tell you how they got here later on.
